claim: The thesis decomposes the problem into SP1-SP3 with Cargo primary.
The method combines optimization, potential games, primal-dual dynamics and explicit interface contracts.
Quota regulation, local Cargo stability, finite route improvement and an information limitation are proved.
SP1/SP2/SP3 empirical headline outcomes hold only in their stated domains.
Cargo completes almost all missions without composing all theoretical mechanisms.
The contribution is a verifiable layered architecture plus planar functional composition.
No global hybrid stability, social optimality, full distribution or industrial validity is proved.
evidence_ref: scope audit and absence of corresponding evidence

Cargo bilateral fixed-contact transport is primary and caging remains separate.

claim: The wrench residual is the SP1-SP2 interface, not proof of full transport.
SP1-SP3 are linked through typed state/information/model contracts.
Cargo repair compares continuing with replacement against stopping, not E6 versus another allocator.
Inference is paired and multiplicity-corrected per predeclared campaign.
A guarantee transfers only if the next layer preserves proof state, information and model.
E2-E4 are reanalyses with missing historical generators; Cargo is regenerable.
MRTA taxonomies do not by themselves solve multi-robot physical feasibility.
evidence_ref: Gerkey/Korsah primary papers plus E3 counterexample

claim: Auction/bundle outputs need an additional common physical closure rule.
Asynchrony, distribution and network robustness are distinct properties.
Arbitrary switching is cited only for individually balanced strongly connected digraphs.
Nedic projection handles convex local constraints but not channel noise.
A variational GNE is a VI solution with common multipliers under regularity.
Resultant wrench and internal forces are distinct under the grasp map.
Safety and progress require distinct endpoints.

claim: MAPF guarantees are model-specific and SP3 uses restricted references.
The quota game is an exact potential game and reaches exact quota Nash under sufficient penalty.
Fair strict better response terminates within the finite-profile bound.
Global potential maximizers minimize cost over exact quota assignments.
The marginal heterogeneous field is the gradient of the declared potential in each unsaturated region.
The unscaled flat field is generally not integrable under heterogeneous capacities.
E2 cannot regenerate world creation because its historical generator is absent.
Coverage and completion objectives produce different empirical tradeoffs.
The marginal correction improves the sequential rule in the paired ablation.
The executed primal-dual variant underperforms greedy in completion.
The regularized residual is conservative: acceptance implies pure feasibility, but feasible points may be rejected.
The E3 relaxed shared-constraint game has the declared potential and variational GNE/KKT equivalence.
The vector wrench guard removes observed scalar false positives.
evidence_ref: E3 audited results and generated macros

claim: The unicycle-to-wheel bridge respects kinematics and wheel limits.
Adding a robot need not monotonically improve realizable wrench under constraints.
Scalar capacity is insufficient for wrench feasibility.
The fixed-contact pose controller has the stated local dissipativity/stability bound.
Safety filters remove observed docking collisions but increase timeouts.
The small V4 stratum favors the game+CBF combination only descriptively.
Transport controllers exhibit a time-work tradeoff in the reduced planar model.
E4 does not validate end-to-end hybrid stability or independent Coppelia physics.
The guarded binary recovery game is exact potential and finite-improvement.
Above the threshold, pure Nash are exactly feasible inclusion-minimal repairs.
PoS equals one but worst-equilibrium PoA is unbounded.
Recovery duration is bounded only under aggregate activation-window, detection, travel and settling assumptions.
All recoverable static certificates restore and impossible reserves do not reopen.
Tight deadlines expose a negative performance result for the potential rule.
Cargo tests functional coexistence, not automatic composition of SP1/SP2 guarantees.
Cargo achieves .997 mission success in the reduced planar benchmark.
The combined physical-guard block improves success only over three nonnominal regimes and its intersection statistic aggregates four.
Continuing with replacement improves failure-regime success versus stopping.
The timing contrast is inconclusive after Holm correction.
The finite route game is exact potential and every maximal strict-improvement path ends at Nash.
Conflict-free Nash follows only under unilateral accessibility and a sufficient penalty.
No-starvation is conditional on finite ordering, release and no re-entry.
Local reservation restores delivery in the tested discrete catalogue.
The restricted oracle is faster in makespan; comparison excludes CBS/ECBS/ORCA.
AWS Industrial 2 is a geometric/kinematic pilot, not dynamic validation.
Congested pilot scenarios fail to deliver despite sampled overlap exclusion.
The main research question has only a conditional answer.
Cargo supports functional compatibility rather than integrated validation of SP1-SP2.
RQ1 is supported only for exact quota and marginal alignment; QR remains inactive.
Hypotheses H1b/H1c/H5b are not adjudicated; H2/H4/HP are explicitly bounded.
evidence_ref: conclusion hypothesis table and active graph
